Over the long-term, we expect demand for TiO 2 will grow by 2% to 3% per year, consistent with our expectations for the long-term growth in GDP.

Additionally, we estimate that changes in currency exchange rates (primarily the euro) increased our Chemicals Segment’s net sales by approximately $39 million in the first nine months of 2026 as compared to the first nine months of 2025.

We estimate that changes in currency exchange rates decreased operating income by approximately $5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, as discussed in the effects of currency exchange rates section below.

We estimate that changes in currency exchange rates decreased operating income by approximately $23 million in the first nine months of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, as discussed in the effects of currency exchange rates section below.
Outlook – During the third quarter of 2026, our Chemicals Segment continued the positive momentum from the first half of the year, with sales volumes improving compared to the same period in 2025.

Our Chemicals Segment’s order backlog entering the fourth quarter remains favorable compared to the prior year, and combined with planned maintenance activities at several of our Chemicals Segment’s facilities, it expects its finished goods inventory levels to remain below normal.

Based on our Chemicals Segment’s performance during the first nine months of 2026, our Chemicals Segment expects full-year net sales and sales volumes to exceed 2025 levels, and it expects gross margin and operating income margins to improve compared to 2025.

Our Chemicals Segment implemented additional price increases during the second and third quarters of 2026 in response to higher production, energy and distribution costs, and, based on price increases our Chemicals Segment has announced to its customers and continued cost pressures, our Chemicals Segment expects its average TiO2 selling prices in the fourth quarter of 2026 to be improved.

Our Chemicals Segment operated its facilities within its normal capacity range during the first nine months of 2026, and our Chemicals Segment currently expects to continue operating within its normal capacity range for the remainder of the year.

Our Chemicals Segment also continues to pursue targeted sales growth opportunities in regions affected by logistical challenges and trade measures that have reduced the competitiveness of certain imports.
While our Chemicals Segment typically experiences significant seasonal cash usage in the first half of the year, it expects liquidity to improve over the remainder of 2026.
Our Chemicals Segment will continue to actively manage working capital, including inventories and receivables, to bolster operating cash flows and maintain financial flexibility.

Our Chemicals Segment believes availability under its revolving credit facility, combined with the absence of near-term debt maturities and improved operating cash flows, will provide adequate liquidity for expected working capital needs and capital allocation priorities.

Outlook – Our Component Products Segment’s results for the first nine months of 2026 reflected higher sales and improved profitability in both the security products and marine components reporting units.

Our Component Products Segment expects these favorable trends to continue throughout the remainder of 2026 and it expects net sales, gross margin and operating income for the full year of 2026 to exceed 2025 levels.

To support these favorable demand trends and anticipated growth opportunities, our Component Products Segment is making targeted investments, primarily in its marine components reporting unit, to expand capacity, enhance operational capabilities and improve overall efficiency, including increased personnel levels and capital expenditures.

Although demand remains favorable across many of our Component Products Segment’s end markets, it will continue to monitor economic conditions and customer ordering patterns for signs of slowing activity in certain sectors.
We expect the development work to be completed by the end of 2027.

Because we recognize revenue over time using cost-based inputs, we will continue to recognize revenue on land previously sold over the development period, even though we have already received all the cash proceeds related to these sales.
We currently expect to recognize substantially all remaining deferred revenue by the end of 2027.
We expect 2026 land development costs to be lower than those in 2025 primarily due to delays in approvals for planned infrastructure projects and the availability of certain construction materials.
We expect to receive cash payments on the related notes receivable over the next 5 to 7 years.

Overall, we currently expect that our net general corporate expenses in 2026 will be higher than in 2025 primarily due to expected increases in litigation fees and related costs, predominantly in the fourth quarter of the year.

If our current expectations regarding the number of cases in which we expect to be involved during 2026, or the nature of such cases were to change, our corporate expenses could be higher than we currently estimate.

Obligations for environmental remediation and related costs are difficult to assess and estimate and it is possible that actual costs for environmental remediation and related costs will exceed accrued amounts or that costs will be incurred in the future for sites in which we cannot currently estimate the liability.
We expect interest expense will be higher in 2026 as compared to 2025 primarily due to higher average debt balances and higher interest rates on Kronos’ debt issued in the third quarter of 2025.

We have previously concluded no valuation allowance is required to be recognized with respect to such carryforwards principally because (i) such carryforwards have an indefinite carryforward period, (ii) we have utilized a portion of such carryforwards during the most recent three-year period and (iii) we currently expect to utilize the remainder of such carryforwards over the long term.

As noted in our discussion of our Real Estate Management and Development segment above, we have sold all of the land in our residential/planned community, and in accordance with our development agreement with the City of Henderson and our contractual obligations with builders, we expect to complete our land development obligations over the next two years.
Because we have largely received cash proceeds from land sales, we expect LandWell to generate negative operating cash flows as it completes its required land development work.

The declaration and payment of future dividends, and the amount thereof, is discretionary and is dependent upon a number of factors including our current and future expected results of operations, financial condition, cash requirements for our businesses, contractual and other requirements and restrictions and other factors deemed relevant by our board of directors.

From time-to-time we will incur indebtedness, generally to (i) fund short-term working capital needs, (ii) refinance existing indebtedness, (iii) make investments in marketable and other securities (including the acquisition of securities issued by our subsidiaries and affiliates) or (iv) fund major capital expenditures or the acquisition of other assets outside the ordinary course of business.

We routinely compare our liquidity requirements and alternative uses of capital against the estimated future cash flows we expect to receive from our subsidiaries, and the estimated sales value of those units.
We intend to consider such acquisition activities in the future and, in connection with this activity, may consider issuing additional equity securities and increasing indebtedness.

Based upon our expectations of our operating performance, and the anticipated demands on our cash resources, we expect to have sufficient liquidity to meet our short-term (defined as the twelve-month period ending September 30, 2027) and long-term obligations (defined as the five-year period ending September 30, 2031).
